ranking_by: average distance from Earth over time
title: The 5 Planets Closest to Earth on Average, Ranked (#1 Isn't Venus)

scenes.text: The planets closest to Earth, on average. Venus doesn't win.
Number five: Saturn. On average, about nine and a half times the Earth-Sun distance.
scenes.label: Saturn · 9.5 AU

scenes.text: Number four: Jupiter. About five times farther from us than the Sun, on average.
scenes.label: Jupiter · 5.2 AU

scenes.text: Number three: Mars. About 1.7 times the Earth-Sun distance, averaged over time.
scenes.label: Mars · 1.7 AU

scenes.text: Number two: Venus. It gets closest of all, but spends long stretches on the far side of the Sun.
scenes.label: Venus · 1.14 AU

scenes.text: Number one: Mercury. It never strays far from the Sun, so it's never that far from us.
scenes.label: Mercury · 1.04 AU

description:
Averaged over time, Mercury, not Venus, is Earth's closest planet, according to a 2019 calculation published in Physics Today.
Venus comes closest at its nearest approach, but it spends much of its orbit on the far side of the Sun. Mercury's small orbit keeps it near the Sun, and so never too far from anyone.
Which planet would you have put at number one?
first_comment: Did you have Venus at number one? Mercury is actually the closest planet on average to every planet. What should we rank next?
